metadata.caption_reason: Rithika chose to skip captions; the compiler has no burn-in step.
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: Rithika, 2026-10-10: the hesitant writer, key terms card and Your Turn composer are skipped. (1) Runtime: the pitch has a hard 4:00 maximum and her narration alone measures about 3:40, so ~40 s of bookends would push it over. (2) Branding: those components carry the instructor's identity (the instructor's narrator greeting and channel handle on the folder labels), which this student film may not show. (3) Beats 1-3 already do their jobs: beat 1 is the hook/question, beats 2-3 define the terms. The outro is never exempt: beat 14 is BOUT, drawn in Manim with her own title and handle.
metadata.people_rule: Cartoon people authorised by Rithika (2026-10-11): generic flat figures drawn in Manim (ME/Rithika, keyword librarian = BM25, meaning librarian = embedding, lazy librarian, searcher, reviewer). No portrait, likeness or name of the instructor; the toolkit's portrait house rule does not apply to this student film. The robot stays the AI agent.
metadata.constructed_rule: Beats flagged constructed=true carry an on-screen CONSTRUCTED label (B03, B06B, B09, B12); real data carries a small source tag.
metadata.audience: complete beginners and the INFO 7375 grader; hiring managers later

beats.script_text: Picture asking a question online. More and more, an AI assistant does the searching for you. But it doesn't type your question. It rewrites it into several searches of its own. My project asks one thing: when the AI writes the search, does the right answer still come back?

beats.script_text: I'm Rithika, and this is Agentic Retrieval Lab. When it's done, it will be a public GitHub repository: a Python pipeline, tests, dated result files, and a short write-up of where search fails. "Agentic" here means agent-written queries. I'm not building an autonomous agent.

beats.script_text: Some of it already exists. This week I took 300 real search questions from the public MS MARCO dataset, had Claude Haiku rewrite each into four agent-style searches, indexed all 8.8 million passages, and built a 200,000-passage test set. 103 tests pass.

beats.script_text: I looked at two alternatives. Perplexity's Q2D-Web paper studies agent searches over 190 million documents, but its data is private; the public gets a leaderboard, not the data. MS MARCO is public, but its questions are written by humans, with about one answer each.

beats.script_text: That paper found something surprising: on its main measure, the keyword librarian scores lowest, yet finds the most books no one else finds. It suggests testing whether the two work better as a team. My project will run that test at small scale, on public data, on one laptop, with every number traceable to a file.

beats.script_text: What could sink it: in my test set, the decoys the keyword librarian picked average about 65 words, and the correct passages about 54. A librarian who simply grabs short books could look smarter than it is. So first, I'll test a lazy librarian that only picks short passages. If it beats random, I'll fix the test set before trusting any ranking.
